Based on the data you provided, the short answer is: **No, you will not be able to see the Moon.**

Here is the breakdown of why, based on the astronomical coordinates:

### 1. The Altitude (The most important factor)
The Moon’s altitude is listed as **-51.919 degrees**. 
*   An altitude of **0 degrees** means the Moon is exactly on the horizon.
*   A **negative** altitude means the Moon is physically below the horizon.
*   At nearly -52 degrees, the Moon is deep below the horizon. To see it, you would essentially need to be standing in a very deep canyon or looking through a massive amount of earth/ocean.

### 2. The Azimuth (Direction)
The azimuth is **275.986 degrees**. 
*   In navigation, 270 degrees is due West. 
*   This means that even if the Moon were above the horizon, it would be positioned in the Western sky. However, because the altitude is so deeply negative, it is currently "setting" (or has already set) well below the western horizon.

### 3. Illumination and Distance
While the Moon is 5.75% illuminated (a very thin crescent), this doesn't matter for visibility because of its position. Even if it were a Full Moon, it would still be invisible because it is physically blocked by the curvature of the Earth.

### Summary for your location (Perth):
At 19:25 AWST on July 12, 2026, the Moon is currently on the opposite side of the Earth relative to your position. You would have to wait several hours for it to rise into the eastern sky.
